title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Alternative Methods - Pilot Programs
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency implements a pilot program to test a new automated traffic enforcement technology from a specific vendor. After a successful 6-month trial, the agency decides to deploy the technology city-wide. What is the standard procurement requirement for the city-wide deployment?
options: The agency can award directly to the pilot vendor since the technology is proven
The agency must use an emergency purchase to avoid losing the trial setup
The agency must issue a competitive solicitation (e.g., RFP) to allow all market participants to compete
The pilot vendor must be excluded from the subsequent competition to avoid a conflict of interest
questions.explain: A pilot or trial procurement is typically a small-scale, limited-duration test. It cannot be used to bypass competition for a permanent, full-scale implementation; a formal competitive process must follow.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A key risk of utilizing a Pilot Program with a specific vendor prior to issuing a formal RFP is:
options: The vendor may gain an unfair competitive advantage or inside information for the ensuing RFP
The agency cannot legally publish an RFP after a pilot
The pilot automatically converts into a sole source agreement
The Brooks Act requires the pilot to be awarded to the lowest bidder
questions.explain: Incumbency and inside knowledge gained during a pilot can skew the upcoming RFP. Buyers must ensure the pilot vendor does not write the RFP specifications and that all competitors get equal information.
